viewpoints.name: Residential Street
viewpoints.purpose: A peaceful residential street near the family home

viewpoints.name: Walk-in: Apartment Lobby
viewpoints.purpose: Eight metres from the street door of an apartment building, facing it. Hold W to walk up: the door opens, and inside are a lobby with a stair, mailboxes and a bench and a corridor behind doors that open. Almost every other door on the street opens onto a bare hall.

viewpoints.name: Glider: Take-off Run
viewpoints.purpose: The hang glider waits on the residential street 16 m short of the lift plaza, facing back along the hero street with 470 m of clear road ahead. Hold W to roll, press Space to climb off, T for manual flight, R to drop a ball (docs/36 section 3.5).

viewpoints.name: Glider: Over the City
viewpoints.purpose: In flight 300 m above the floor of the first rotor, flying with the spin at 14 m/s: the pilot feels about 1.1 g at this height. W and S set speed, A and D turn, Space and C climb and descend, R drops a ball (docs/36 section 3.5).

viewpoints.name: Groundside Park
viewpoints.purpose: A spacious lakeside park framed by low-rise housing and distant curved city: the family lake and its park, 220 m from the family home (plan block 683), seen along the park path toward the water.

viewpoints.name: Arbor Brook: The Spring
viewpoints.purpose: The knoll top above the spring pool of Arbor Brook, the axis of the park running away to the end wall over the meadow and the planted belt.

viewpoints.name: Arbor Brook: Stepping Stones
viewpoints.purpose: The meadow run of Arbor Brook from the bank by the stepping stones, looking upstream to the knoll along a shallow stream between soft banks.

viewpoints.name: Arbor Brook: The Glen
viewpoints.purpose: The glen path at the second pool of Arbor Brook, looking downstream where the stream drops through small steps under the canopy.

viewpoints.name: Arbor Brook: The Falls
viewpoints.purpose: The falls terrace at the lower end of Arbor Brook: the stream leaves the glen over a drop of 2.4 m into a plunge pool, with the city climbing the curve of the rotor behind.

viewpoints.name: Arbor Brook: Overfly Start (QA)
viewpoints.purpose: First key of the S38 brook overfly: 0.4 m over the water of the glen reach, facing downstream. Capture view with no site page.

viewpoints.name: District Skyline
viewpoints.purpose: The landmark skyline at eye height: a cluster of crowned towers, spires and a signature landmark seen from a park lawn 1.1 km away (docs/32 city landmarks; QA `city-landmarks:qa --mode capture`).

viewpoints.name: Civic Landmark
viewpoints.purpose: A town hall with its clock tower and portico from the street in front of it: the close view of the civic landmark catalogue (docs/32).

viewpoints.name: Urban Megaframe Base
viewpoints.purpose: See a foundational rib rise from a lived-in groundside neighborhood.

viewpoints.name: Mid-Gravity Megaframe
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect bay infill, partial decks, bridges, and the frame at roughly 0.55 g.

viewpoints.name: Low-G Atrium
viewpoints.purpose: Look across long-span structure and sparse atmospheric process facilities at roughly 0.32 g.

viewpoints.name: Megaframe Plate District
viewpoints.purpose: Stand on a raised 625 m plate quarter (about 0.73 g, rotor 1, bay 35): the balustrade and planters of the deck edge, an inhabited bridge with its truss crossing the ring beam, block rows on the next plate, and, because the plate stands above the 450 m sky, the opposite upper city overhead.

viewpoints.name: End Wall: Foot of the Cliff
viewpoints.purpose: Stand in the end bay of rotor 1 at the foot of its +X end wall (zone W, docs/27): the cantilevered ledges with their coffered undersides and struts, a train viaduct crossing the frame, the planted cliff face rising to the sky seam.

viewpoints.name: End Wall: Viaduct Terrace
viewpoints.purpose: Stand on the 241 m viaduct ledge of the +X end wall of rotor 1 (about 0.9 g): a train on the track strip, balustrade and planters with trailing vines, a glazed hall and terraced blocks on the ledge, the city 240 m below.

viewpoints.name: End Wall: Sky Balcony
viewpoints.purpose: Walk out along a timber boardwalk to an overlook on the +X end wall of rotor 1, 342 m up and about 50 m under the artificial sky (0.86 g): a glass handrail, benches, lamps, viewing scopes and a plaque, with the whole city laid out below and the sky membrane overhead.

viewpoints.name: End Wall: Upper Wall from the Axis Side
viewpoints.purpose: Look at the upper end wall of rotor 1 from about 2,150 m (0.14 g): concentric ledge rings with low-gravity halls, vaults and gardens, the ribs thinning toward the bore, the ground city and megaframe below.

viewpoints.name: Upper City Fringe
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect atmospheric process vaults, nutrient vessels and grow galleries above the opaque sky backing.

viewpoints.name: Axis Station Plaza
viewpoints.purpose: Show the groundside neighborhood plaza and boarding lift entrance.

viewpoints.name: Ascender — 250 m
viewpoints.purpose: Early transition: the neighborhood remains familiar as the horizon rises.

viewpoints.name: Ascender — Artificial Sky Breakthrough
viewpoints.purpose: Signature reveal of the engineered sky, opposite city, and open interior.

viewpoints.name: Ascender — Cabin Interior
viewpoints.purpose: Ride inside the panoramic cabin at 650 m (0.74 g): window seats, rails, the glass floor gallery and the live altitude, gravity and transfer display, with the city curving up beyond the glass (docs/21).

viewpoints.name: Ascender — Tower From Outside
viewpoints.purpose: Stand 140 m beside the tower at 800 m altitude: four blade trusses with bronze lattice, three tracks with cabins climbing and descending, belt-truss nodes and the axis far above (docs/21).

viewpoints.name: Ascender — Rotating Transfer Hub
viewpoints.purpose: From the stationary spine: the rotor 1 transfer hub drum turning behind its bearing collar, the four tower portals with their bronze sunbursts, and the spin-decoupling chambers (docs/21 section 7).

viewpoints.name: Spin-Decoupling Lock, Tsiolkovsky
viewpoints.purpose: Inside the spine at the rotor 1 hub, mid spin-down: the lock liner with its viewing slots and door portals over the eight-chamber carousel, the amber indicator ring and the spin-rate display (docs/28 section 5).

viewpoints.name: Ascender — Near Axis
viewpoints.purpose: Show the final transition from the distant city to zero-g infrastructure.

viewpoints.name: Stationary Axis — City Rotating Around Viewer
viewpoints.purpose: Canonical reference-frame view with the city rotating around a slender spine.

viewpoints.name: Axial Spine — Interior
viewpoints.purpose: From the axis beside the rotor 1 hub, down the 120 m stationary tube: frames and ring lamps every 25 m, the express guideway on its stays, the crew galleries, the four trunks and the AXIS 01 boards (docs/28 section 3).

viewpoints.name: Axial Spine — Observation Windows
viewpoints.purpose: From the +z crew gallery in a panoramic segment of rotor 1 (1 km before the hub): the arched windows with the rotating city turning past beyond the still spine.

viewpoints.name: Axial Spine — Refuge Capsule
viewpoints.purpose: A pressure refuge in the rotor 2 stretch of the spine: hatch and handwheel, amber beacon, lit ports, tether rail down to the crew gallery, refuge boards.

viewpoints.name: Inter-Rotor Service Gap
viewpoints.purpose: Expose the vacuum gap, rotor ends, bearings, and service connections.

viewpoints.name: Inter-Rotor Bridge 01, Outside
viewpoints.purpose: The transit bridge between rotors 01 and 02 from its sunlit flank, 2,300 m from the axis: window bands and X bracing, the lenticular lower truss on the hull side, the mid-span telescope and the gimbal ends at the port collars.

viewpoints.name: Inter-Rotor Bridge 01, Deck
viewpoints.purpose: On the deck of bridge 01, 50 m from rotor 01: the promenade, the transit lane with its guideway and shuttle, window bands both sides, distance markers and the far pressure door.

viewpoints.name: Bridge Port, Tsiolkovsky
viewpoints.purpose: The street side of rotor 01's bridge port: the lit ring, bronze bezel and sunburst architrave, the parked shielding leaves on their rails and, through the port, the bridge deck.

viewpoints.name: Counter-Rotating Interface, Noordung and Bernal
viewpoints.purpose: Show the gap between rotors that spin opposite ways: no rotating bridge, a stationary service frame and slip seals. Passengers cross through the spine.

viewpoints.name: Axial Express · Interior
viewpoints.purpose: Inside car 02 on the centre line the story rides, down the aisle: restraint couches on the four wall quarters, grab rails and poles, net-door lockers, the live destination display over the open end door (docs/28 section 4).

viewpoints.name: Axial Express · Panoramic Bay
viewpoints.purpose: A panoramic bay of car 02 (bay 5): the full-height side window and the roof light looking out at the spine (tech spec 21: panoramic windows in selected sections).

viewpoints.name: Axial Express · On the Guideway
viewpoints.purpose: The five-car express on its guideway in the spine, three-quarter view from ahead of the head car: cab nose, destination board, gangways, levitation bogies, running lights.

viewpoints.name: Aft Works · Panoramic Aft Gallery
viewpoints.purpose: The AFT TERMINUS platform with the express standing at it, looking aft through the glazed end wall: the free run, the 120 m service port, the 350 m bore and the blast iris (docs/38 section 11).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works · Aft Terminus Platform
viewpoints.purpose: Along the AFT TERMINUS boarding platform toward the standing express: the gate frames at the car doors, hazard edge and lamp strip, the terminus boards and the transfer-lock hatches in the tube wall (docs/38 section 11).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works · Service Bay
viewpoints.purpose: Inside the vacuum service bay beside the tube: tug, servicing craft and tender on their cradles, the transfer gangways, a lifeboat, the shell with its work lights and the aft wall with the service port (docs/38 section 11).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works · Tsiolkovsky Aft Bearing Gallery
viewpoints.purpose: The aft hub bearing of rotor 1 (docs/15): sleeve and rim turning against the stator, catchers, alignment actuators, the slip-seal labyrinth and the service frame, the rotor 04 pattern mirrored (docs/38 section 11).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works · Converter Hall
viewpoints.purpose: Through the arched windows of the spine: rows of HVDC valve halls, breaker bays, capacitor banks, cooling headers and the structural rings of the converter hall (docs/38 section 11).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works · Aft Operations
viewpoints.purpose: The control blister and the black-start switchgear hall on the tube, with the reactor feed leaving for the masts (docs/38 section 11).

viewpoints.name: Bearing Gallery · Counter-Rotation
viewpoints.purpose: Show rotor 04 and the industrial rotor turning in opposite directions about the stationary spine and hub bearings.

viewpoints.name: Momentum Control Bay
viewpoints.purpose: From above ring 1 near the rotor 04 end wall, look along the bay: the four reaction rings in their housings (catwalks, bearing stacks, struts to the spine clamps, ring boards), the stationary spine and the industrial frame beyond (docs/28 section 6; moved into the bay 2026-10-08, the old pose was inside rotor 04).

viewpoints.name: Momentum Ring 2 · Close
viewpoints.purpose: Under ring 2 on the axis side: the containment housing and its ribs, motor-generator stators, a bearing stack, coolant loops, the catwalk edge and the rim turning in the open side (docs/28 section 6).

viewpoints.name: Ehricke Industrial Rotor, Wide
viewpoints.purpose: Establish the open truss, vacuum volumes, cargo, and robotic logistics.

viewpoints.name: Upper City Agriculture
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect atmospheric stacked crops, nutrient equipment, and robotic harvesters.

viewpoints.name: Farm Grow Deck
viewpoints.purpose: Stand in the visitor gallery of the grow hall and look along a deck: racks of lettuce, basil and kale in four growth stages, LED rigs, nutrient channels, a harvest gantry.

viewpoints.name: Farm Harvest Line
viewpoints.purpose: Watch totes arrive on the belt and pass the wash tunnel, the optical sorter and the weigher in the process wing.

viewpoints.name: Farm Packaging and Dispatch
viewpoints.purpose: See ordinary food (crates of salad, trays of loaves, bottles, wrapped pallets) leave on freight pods from the process wing dock.

viewpoints.name: Service Facilities at 1,000 m
viewpoints.purpose: See a grow gallery and a utility plant of the 1,000 m service tier from the open fringe: glazed rack faces lit white and magenta, vessels, air handlers and pipe racks.

viewpoints.name: Zero-G Shipyard — Hero View
viewpoints.purpose: Reveal the unsupported spacecraft inside a much larger construction volume.

viewpoints.name: Shipyard — Close Construction View
viewpoints.purpose: Material and robotics QA on framing, tankage, hull, and temporary fixtures.

viewpoints.name: Shipyard — Open Pressure Section
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect the open crew drum (deck stack), capture arms, a manipulator and an inspection capsule at working range.

viewpoints.name: Shipyard — Tank Bay and Delivery
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect the tank cradles, a tank on approach with its mover, tension lines, crawlers and umbilicals.

viewpoints.name: Passenger Spaceport Terminal
viewpoints.purpose: Show Concordia passenger arrivals, terminal identity signage, zero-g public infrastructure, and docking views.

viewpoints.name: Spaceport Axial Bay
viewpoints.purpose: Keep the axial approach clear while showing docked craft and approach lighting.

viewpoints.name: Spaceport Arrival Face
viewpoints.purpose: Arrive through the link tube to the WELCOME TO CONCORDIA arch, then the health, customs and security rings of the processing zone.

viewpoints.name: Spaceport Concourse A
viewpoints.purpose: Show the nave: the deck with its shops, the handline conveyors with their riders, the catch-net rings and the gate arches along the bay windows.

viewpoints.name: Spaceport Gate A03
viewpoints.purpose: A gate with its boarding bridge, berth frame and a docked passenger craft, seen from the axial bay.

viewpoints.name: Spaceport Rotating Lounges
viewpoints.purpose: The three rotating comfort lounges (0.13, 0.20 and 0.28 g) on their stationary hubs, seen through the nave windows.

viewpoints.name: Spaceport External Pier
viewpoints.purpose: Pier P1 on the outer face of the end bulkhead with a freighter alongside, tugs and the axial aperture.

viewpoints.name: Passenger Launcher Interior
viewpoints.purpose: Verify the 98-couch passenger cabin, its window band, aisle lighting and shelter bulkhead, seen standing in the starboard aisle.

viewpoints.name: Launcher Track — External
viewpoints.purpose: Show the electromagnetic track and gantries as transport infrastructure.

viewpoints.name: Shuttle Bay — Concordia Shuttle
viewpoints.purpose: Walk round a Concordia shuttle parked on the launch track: ivory hull, stowed arrays and radiators, the keel in its guideway, edge lights, floodlight masts and bay signage.

viewpoints.name: Shuttle Bay — Inside the Cabin
viewpoints.purpose: Step inside the shuttle parked in bay 1: the 98-couch cabin, window band and aisle lighting, empty between flights.

viewpoints.name: Shuttle Bay 2 — Inside the Cabin
viewpoints.purpose: The cabin of the shuttle parked in bay 2, identical to bay 1 and empty between flights.

viewpoints.name: Shuttle Bay 3 — Inside the Cabin
viewpoints.purpose: The cabin of the shuttle parked in bay 3, identical to bay 1 and empty between flights.

viewpoints.name: Exterior Hull — Close Inspection
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect shielding cassettes, repair seams, the maintenance rail and the service robot at an open slot.

viewpoints.name: Aft Observatory — Tower Crown
viewpoints.purpose: The pressure sphere on the aft tower crown, with the iris and the tower behind it (docs/specs/aft-lounge-spec.md).

viewpoints.name: Aft Observatory — Inside, Pole Window
viewpoints.purpose: Inside the aft observatory, looking down the axis through the pole window past the grab pole.

viewpoints.name: Exterior Hero — Complete Habitat
viewpoints.purpose: Opening composition with the entire habitat, Earth, and Moon in view.

viewpoints.name: Exterior Hero — Complete Habitat
viewpoints.purpose: Canonical silhouette of the entire stationary habitat and attached utilities.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — Industrial Open Bay
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect the exposed counter-rotating industrial rotor through its open-vacuum shell bay.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — Aft End Lighting
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect the shaded end cap and its mounted service floodlights.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — Spaceport Approach
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect the Concordia arrival mark and look through the axial docking aperture at the berths and approaching craft.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA: Open Port Frame
viewpoints.purpose: Look at the open port from 6 km off the axis: the port frame (spokes, mid and inner pier rings), the terminal citadel, the piers and the cage running back toward the yard (docs/specs/forward-port-spec.md).

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA: Shipyard Through the Cage
viewpoints.purpose: Look from outside, off the sun-shade side, through the open forward cage at the hero ship, the yard ribs and the cage frames (docs/35).

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — 25 km Silhouette
viewpoints.purpose: Check the sunlit three-quarter silhouette, radiator farms, and port against a black cislunar sky.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — Propellant Farm
viewpoints.purpose: Check the tank farm (two LH2 and two LOX foil spheres, two storable cylinders), sunshades, radiators, transfer lines and exclusion posts from the outboard side.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — 5 km Systems
viewpoints.purpose: Check major shielding zones, structural bands, utility trunks, and radiator scale.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — 1 km Patchwork
viewpoints.purpose: Check shielding patchwork, access systems, port structures, and service infrastructure.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — 200 m Engineering Detail
viewpoints.purpose: Check the hull as layered infrastructure without introducing greeble noise.

viewpoints.name: Exterior QA — 25 m Materials
viewpoints.purpose: Inspect cartridge frames, repairs, service rail, thermal plumbing, serial markings, and the crawler.

viewpoints.name: Radiator Field
viewpoints.purpose: Show a radiator bank from the hull side: pylons, spine, ribs, panel backs, headers, and habitat scale.

viewpoints.name: Radiator Mount
viewpoints.purpose: Show how a radiator pylon stands on the hull: shoes on rib intersections, truss legs, hub, manifold house and risers.

viewpoints.name: Radiator Spine and Hinge
viewpoints.purpose: Close view under a radiator bank: spine truss, hinge housing, supply and return headers, ribs and panel backs with edge headers and valves.

viewpoints.name: Backup PV Collector
viewpoints.purpose: Show the modest backup PV collector: four-leg mast on hull shoes, gimbal, bus truss and tracking wings.

viewpoints.name: RF Dish Station
viewpoints.purpose: Show an RF dish station: shoe, lattice tower, turntable and yoke, Cassegrain reflector, equipment hut, optical terminal and phased arrays.

viewpoints.name: Forward Defence Battery
viewpoints.purpose: Show the forward launcher battery: armoured housing, reload magazine, rapid-interceptor cells, net launcher, blast wall, hazard apron, Whipple skirt and the sensor group beyond (docs/33).

viewpoints.name: Aft Sensor Cluster
viewpoints.purpose: Show an aft sensor group: radar fence faces on their A-frame, tracking dish, survey telescopes, lidar masts and the fire-control hub (docs/33).

viewpoints.name: Launcher Housing (Readiness Drill)
viewpoints.purpose: Close view of a launcher housing during its scheduled readiness drill: shutters open, interceptor rails slewed to the pinned drill sector, point-defence guns sweeping; nothing is fired (docs/33).

viewpoints.name: Metro Platform — Arbor
viewpoints.purpose: Arbor ring station (docs/30): the 108 m platform on the hump at 55 m, screen doors, the canopy and the set at the platform.

viewpoints.name: Metro Viaduct Over an Arterial
viewpoints.purpose: Eye height on the circumferential arterial: the 45 m viaduct overhead on its portals, the line running away along the street (docs/30).

viewpoints.name: Metro Station From the Street
viewpoints.purpose: Looking up the arterial at an interchange: the pier with its street entrance, the viaduct climbing the hump to the station (docs/30).

viewpoints.name: Metro Axis West Platform
viewpoints.purpose: The Axis West platform beside the ascender keep-out, looking toward the ascender base along the axial viaduct (docs/30).

viewpoints.name: Metro Lift Tower — Arbor
viewpoints.purpose: The glass lift tower of the hero story at the Arbor crossing (docs/30 section 14): the street door and canopy, the shaft rising 46 m to the platform deck, the viaduct above.

viewpoints.name: Metro Interchange — 625 m Beam Line
viewpoints.purpose: The 625 m beam line interchange on the ring beam (docs/30): the platform at 0.75 g with the glazed bore side and the set at the platform.

viewpoints.name: Solar Infrastructure
viewpoints.purpose: Show the tethered solar farm (power platform P1 at the docs/38 farm hub) with the aft face and its HVDC tethers beyond.

viewpoints.name: Power Platform — Flagship
viewpoints.purpose: P1 from 4 km on the Sun side: the PV field, truss and bus at the docs/38 farm hub, with the aft face and its tethers as the reference.

viewpoints.name: Power Platform — Bus
viewpoints.purpose: P1 from 200 m above the sunlit side of the bus: the P1 marking and the gold tanks, the tether boom with its eight HVDC reel houses on the front face, and the reel leads fanning out to the docs/38 tethers.

viewpoints.name: Power Platform — Rear
viewpoints.purpose: P1 from 3.2 km behind and below the array plane, looking back toward the station: the unlit blanket backs framing the bus under its work lights, and the aft face beyond with the HVDC tethers running to the platform.

viewpoints.name: Volatiles Depot — Tug Port
viewpoints.purpose: V1 from 180 m off the +Z keel end: a tug-port collar on the keel side, a white water tank under the shade with the work-light pools on it, the gold mesh dish and a PV wing.

viewpoints.name: Power Platform — Night Side
viewpoints.purpose: P1 from the anti-Sun side with only Earth light and the lamps: the bus outline, the truss line and at least 12 lamps.

viewpoints.name: Satellite Fleet — Opening Shot
viewpoints.purpose: The opening-shot camera (the exterior-intro pose) with the fleet around the station; V2 is in frame, P1 is not (see sat-fleet-hero-p1).

viewpoints.name: Satellite Fleet — Opening Shot With P1
viewpoints.purpose: The opening-shot position turned toward P1 so that the station and the power platform share the frame, at a flash of the P1 bus strobe (docs/37 SAT16).

viewpoints.name: Bag Hauler — Under Tow
viewpoints.purpose: The asteroid bag hauler 10.7 km out on its approach, from 155 m off its quarter: the 110 m truss, two 60 m solar wings, radiators and the bag cinched round a 22 m metal chunk (docs/site/facts.md section 11).

viewpoints.name: Bag Hauler — Stern
viewpoints.purpose: The hauler from behind and above its thruster plate: the seven Hall thrusters, propellant tanks, the truss running away toward the bag and the station beyond.

viewpoints.name: Compute Field — The Band
viewpoints.purpose: The compute field from 100 km behind the downlink raft, looking in along the band: rafts of ten dark-blue PV platforms stand in staggered groups across the dark, the station far off in the corner for scale (200 GW, 140 platforms in 14 rafts; economy-scene-spec section 2).

viewpoints.name: Compute Field — Optical Downlink
viewpoints.purpose: The optical downlink D1 at the field centre from 400 m behind it: sixteen 4 m telescopes on shelves at the front of a relay-class bus, all pointed at the Earth, two PV wings on the Sun-tracking joint. No beam is drawn: the watts leave as bits.

viewpoints.name: The Next Station — Yard
viewpoints.purpose: The second station under construction 200 km out: one rotor closed and bare, one in hoop frames, a third of the shield placed, three spinning construction rings, parked bagged asteroids and tugs (economy-scene-spec section 3).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works — Far Read
viewpoints.purpose: The aft end from 25 km, three-quarter on the face: ribbed face, red rim lights, central tower, four landing masts with marker lights, two reactor masts (docs/38).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works — Service Port Approach
viewpoints.purpose: Look along the axis from 3 km at the service port, the blast iris and the tower (docs/38).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works — Power Landing
viewpoints.purpose: The four HVDC landing masts and the tethers running aft to the solar farm hub (docs/38).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works — Reactor Mast
viewpoints.purpose: A black-start reactor on its 800 m mast behind its shadow shield, with the radiator petals edge-on to the Sun (docs/38).

viewpoints.name: Aft Works — Thruster Ring
viewpoints.purpose: The twelve Whipple-shielded thruster pods canted outward on the face ring (docs/38).

viewpoints.name: Post-Launch — Looking Back Home
viewpoints.purpose: Reveal that the enormous armored machine receding behind was home.

viewpoints.name: Earth / Moon / Habitat Context
viewpoints.purpose: Place the habitat in cislunar space without oversized nearby worlds: Earth and Moon above it at their nominal sizes.

viewpoints.name: Racer Dock (R1)
viewpoints.purpose: The two-seat racer on its level launch table atop the spaceport jacket, 10,205 m along the spine, with the ready room, lock tower, boarding gangway, umbilical arms and latches it launches from; it lifts off the dock and leaves through the forward port. B launches it; ?racer=launch starts the sequence on load (docs/specs/exo-racer-spec.md section 6).

viewpoints.name: Shuttle Dock (Gate A03)
viewpoints.purpose: The Concordia shuttle at its berth on gate A03 of the passenger spaceport, nose to the terminal. B then 2 launches it: the arms open, the stack backs out onto the outbound lane and turns, and the controls are yours (docs/specs/flyable-shuttle-spec.md).

viewpoints.name: Shuttle Launch Rail (Sled)
viewpoints.purpose: The Concordia shuttle on the mass-driver sled at the staging point of the launch rail. B then 3 launches it at 1.5 g to the release speed; the controls are yours at the end of the rail (docs/specs/flyable-shuttle-spec.md).

viewpoints.name: Noordung: Civic Street
viewpoints.purpose: A paved civic street in Noordung: a stately frontage on the left, a green square ahead and a tower district on the horizon. Same generator as the first rotor, a different seed and a different city.

viewpoints.name: Noordung: Lakeshore
viewpoints.purpose: A lakeshore promenade in Noordung: reeds and a path at the water, with the plan of the upper city hanging overhead. Each rotor has its own lakes.

viewpoints.name: Noordung: Crowned Towers From 120 m
viewpoints.purpose: The skyline of Noordung from 120 m up: copper-crowned towers and spires at arm's length, with the megaframe and the far side of the world beyond.

viewpoints.name: Bernal: Terrace Street
viewpoints.purpose: A mid-rise terrace street in Bernal at eye height: bike lane, red-roofed terraces and a boulevard running along the rotor into the curve of the city.

viewpoints.name: Bernal: Lakeside Promenade
viewpoints.purpose: A lakeside promenade in Bernal, near its forward end wall: a resident on the path, towers across the water and the upper city overhead.

viewpoints.name: Bernal: Rooftop Panorama From 120 m
viewpoints.purpose: Bernal from 120 m up, looking along the axis: parkland, lakes and mid-rise blocks below, megaframe towers rising to the sky membrane and the curved world beyond.

viewpoints.name: O'Neill: Core Canyon
viewpoints.purpose: A street through the urban core of O'Neill: tall arched frontages close on both sides and the street runs on into the dense center of the district.

viewpoints.name: O'Neill: Lakeside Plaza
viewpoints.purpose: A lakeside plaza in O'Neill: a resident at the water's edge, reeds and trees on the shore and the city rising across the lake and overhead.

viewpoints.name: O'Neill: Tower Field From 120 m
viewpoints.purpose: The urban core of O'Neill from 120 m up: a field of crowned towers and spires, and megaframe ribs climbing toward the sky.

viewpoints.name: Noordung: The Exchange
viewpoints.purpose: The Exchange in the capital quarter of Noordung: a domed market hall behind a portico, seen from 30 m across its plaza. This is where energy and compute are priced and traded for the whole station.

viewpoints.name: Noordung: Charter Hall
viewpoints.purpose: Charter Hall in the capital quarter of Noordung, from the street in front of its portico: the seat of the Concordia Charter Authority, with gate towers and a vaulted roof above the colonnade.

viewpoints.name: Noordung: The Court
viewpoints.purpose: The Court in the capital quarter of Noordung: a columned portico and a pediment on a street of civic frontages, where the station's arbitration courts sit.

viewpoints.name: O'Neill: Garden Villas
viewpoints.purpose: The estates of O'Neill from a raised walk: detached villas on lawns the size of a city block, hedges, planted trees and the megaframe beyond. The richest districts on the station trade density for open ground.

viewpoints.name: O'Neill: Estates and Lake From 60 m
viewpoints.purpose: The estate district of O'Neill from 60 m up: villas in their gardens along a curving street, with a lake and parkland beyond.

viewpoints.name: Ehricke: Tank Farm
viewpoints.purpose: A tank farm on the outer band of the industrial rotor (docs/07 section 43): horizontal vessels and spheres on a lattice deck, seen from inboard of the rail band.

viewpoints.name: Ehricke: Cargo Tug on the Rail
viewpoints.purpose: A cargo tug carrying a pod along an axial rail on the industrial rotor's outer band (docs/07 section 43), close enough to read the load and the lattice rails. The tug shuttles along the rail, so the framing is set for reference time 0.

overlays.name: Gravity
overlays.summary: Gravity here is the push of the floor as the rotor turns. It is 1 g at the ground and falls in a straight line toward the axis, where you float. The artificial sky sits 450 m up at 0.82 g.

overlays.name: Rotational frame
overlays.summary: Tsiolkovsky and Noordung turn one way and Bernal and O'Neill turn the other, each once every 100 seconds. Inside a rotor the ground is still and the stars wheel past. Seen from the spine, the rim moves at 157 m/s.

callouts.text: 0.0626 rad/s, 100 s per turn, 157 m/s rim

overlays.name: Pressure
overlays.summary: The four rotors and the spine hold Earth sea-level air, 101 kPa. The outer shell and the industrial bay are open to vacuum, so each airtight boundary shown here is a wall between the two.

overlays.name: Shielding
overlays.summary: A thick blanket of regolith and slag, packed in cassettes, stops radiation and small debris. A vacuum gap stands off from the hull to take impacts. The shipyard cage and the industrial bay are open, so they carry no blanket.

overlays.name: Thermal
overlays.summary: Nearly all the power the station uses ends up as heat, and radiators are the only way to shed it in space. They reject about 40 GW at 380 to 500 K. Rotary couplings carry heat across the turning joints at the hubs.

callouts.text: Radiators reject about 40 GW at 380 to 500 K
Eight radiator banks stand off the hull
Rotary heat couplings at the hubs

overlays.name: Electrical
overlays.summary: Solar platforms far aft supply about 40 GW, sent in over direct-current lines at plus and minus 1.2 MV. Two fission plants of 250 MWe each can restart the grid from nothing.

overlays.name: Transportation
overlays.summary: A metro ring runs 45 m above the ground in every rotor. Ascenders climb 2,380 m to the hub in about 10 minutes. The spine express covers the long way at 140 m/s, and the launcher on top throws craft toward Earth at 1.5 g.

overlays.name: Material flow
overlays.summary: Regolith, metals, glass and oxygen arrive from the Moon. Iron-nickel, water, carbon and nitrogen arrive from asteroids bagged and hauled to L5, which came first. The industrial rotor stores both, then sends water, air and building stock to the city and hull and tank stock to the yard.

callouts.text: LUNAR FEEDSTOCK: regolith, metals, glass, oxygen
To the city: water, air, building stock
To the yard: hull and tank stock

overlays.name: Structural
overlays.summary: Each rotor is an airtight skin held round by tension bands that carry about 410 MN per metre: 253 from the air, the rest from the weight of the city. Inside, the megaframe rises to 1,500 m above the ground and carries the city. The stationary truss runs the full 21 km.

callouts.text: Rotor tension bands, about 410 MN per metre

overlays.name: Momentum
overlays.summary: Tsiolkovsky and Noordung spin one way and Bernal and O'Neill the other, so the station carries no net spin. Ehricke, the industrial rotor, holds about 4 percent of the total, and the momentum rings cancel it. The net is zero.

callouts.text: Ehricke about 4%, cancelled by momentum rings

overlays.name: Defence
overlays.summary: Four defence sites on the hull, two at each end, watch the approaches. Red marks exclusion zones, amber marks fields of fire and blue marks sensor coverage.

overlays.name: Satellites
overlays.summary: Seven free-flying satellites work around the station. They are a tethered solar farm, two power platforms, two volatiles depots, an Earth relay and a forward sentinel.

hotspots.blurb: Semi-processed stock from the Moon and from captured asteroids waits in the industrial rotor. Heavy tanks sit at the rim, where it weighs 0.45 g.

hotspots.title: Tug on a cargo rail
hotspots.blurb: Robotic tugs about 25 m long run on cargo rails at about 8 m/s. Nothing in the bay is crewed; a person goes in only in a pressurized capsule.

hotspots.title: Meridian 04
hotspots.blurb: Meridian 04 is a 700 m crew and cargo ship under construction. Nothing carries her weight: three lattice rings hold her on pre-tensioned lines.

hotspots.title: The shipyard
hotspots.blurb: Eight rim rings 5 km across frame an open cage around the yard. Ships are built here because a 700 m hull weighs nothing in zero g.

hotspots.title: Comfort lounges
hotspots.blurb: Three rotating lounges at 0.13, 0.20 and 0.28 g rest travellers from weightlessness, with restaurants, sleeping rooms and a quiet deck.

hotspots.title: Arrival face
hotspots.blurb: The arrival face reads WELCOME TO CONCORDIA. Beyond it are health screening, customs with eight lanes and security with eight arches.

hotspots.title: Propellant farm
hotspots.blurb: Two liquid hydrogen spheres, two liquid oxygen spheres and two storable-propellant cylinders sit under sunshades, clear of the approach lane.

hotspots.title: Converter hall
hotspots.blurb: Twelve 50 m bays of HVDC valve halls, breaker bays and capacitor banks turn up to 40 GW of direct current into the supply that feeds the station.

hotspots.title: Aft works
hotspots.blurb: The aft face is a shielded disc with a 350 m tower and blast iris at its centre, four 500 m landing masts and a ring of twelve thruster pods.

hotspots.title: Radiators
hotspots.blurb: Eight radiator banks stand off the hull on pylons and run at 380 to 500 K. Heat can leave a station only as light, so the panels are huge.

hotspots.title: Hull and shielding
hotspots.blurb: The hull is an open truss under shielding cassettes of compacted regolith and slag in 32 m tiles. Mass is the shield.

hotspots.blurb: Four sites guard the station, two forward and two aft. Radar fences, an 85 m tracking dish and interceptor cells watch for debris and answer it.

hotspots.title: Earth
hotspots.blurb: Earth is 384,400 km away. L5 trails the Moon by 60 degrees, a spot where the pull of both bodies and the motion of the orbit balance.

hotspots.title: The Moon
hotspots.blurb: Lunar regolith is 43 percent oxygen by mass. A tonne holds over 400 kg of oxygen plus the metal and stone to build with.
